audit_findings.title: Completed Nalu acquisition creates a perimeter mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $523 million cash paid and $588 million preliminary purchase price; $588 million equals 1.34% of the $43.987 billion base equity value, or $0.40 per supplied diluted share as a scale comparison
audit_findings.mechanism: The latest cash and investment bridge reflects acquisition funding and removal of the prior Nalu stake, while the historical OE anchor excludes Nalu's post-acquisition earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 27, 2026, we completed our acquisition of 100 percent of Nalu Medical, Inc. (Nalu Medical), a privately held medical technology company focused on developing and commercializing innovative and minimally invasive solutions for patients with chronic pain.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its direction is conservative because value-producing Nalu operations are omitted after their purchase consumed cash. Even the entire filed purchase price is only about $0.40 per share, far below the $17.99 gap between market price and base value and the $12.98 gap to bull value, so it cannot reasonably change the valuation conclusion on the supplied scale.
audit_findings.action: At the next annual rerun, include Nalu's post-acquisition OE in the operating perimeter; alternatively, for a strict FY2025-perimeter rerun, restore the $523 million cash payment and $66 million prior-interest value to the bridge without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Penumbra would add unmodeled interest cost and dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $14.500 billion consideration, including approximately $11.000 billion of cash on hand and newly issued debt; interest, issued shares and Penumbra OE are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing would add Penumbra OE, new interest expense, transaction-funded share dilution, and acquisition-related changes to cash, debt and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We plan to fund the transaction consideration through a combination of cash on hand and newly issued debt in an aggregate amount equal to approximately $11.000 billion, and the remaining portion of the transaction consideration will be paid in shares of our common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied record describes Penumbra as pending and the valuation explicitly uses the filed pre-closing perimeter, so the absent financing costs and shares are not a present computational error. The transaction is nevertheless large enough to make the current DCF obsolete upon closing. Its net direction is mixed because Penumbra earnings add value while interest and dilution reduce the existing holders' claim.
audit_findings.action: Confirm closing status through the valuation date. Upon closing, rebuild OE on the combined perimeter, include the actual interest expense and financing terms, replace the share denominator with closing-date fully diluted shares, and reconstruct cash, investments and debt consistently.

audit_findings.title: Historically favorable taxes may not persist through the terminal period
audit_findings.magnitude: $540 million FY2025 tax reduction, equal to 18.4% of the $2.9325 billion OE anchor; exact valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration of jurisdictional incentives raises cash taxes, reducing forecast OE and the terminal earnings base.
audit_findings.evidence: These tax benefits are conditional upon meeting certain thresholds required under statutory law and will expire between fiscal years 2028 and 2034, unless extended.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization issue: filed incentives expire between 2028 and 2034, while nearly half of base operating value comes from the terminal period. The FY2025 benefit is large relative to the OE anchor, so perpetuating the historically favorable burden is reasonably capable of materially overstating value. The exact reduction cannot be established without jurisdictional earnings and tax forecasts.
audit_findings.action: Build a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction cash-tax schedule reflecting each expiration, including Costa Rica through 2033, and rerun every scenario and terminal value using the resulting normalized OE.

audit_findings.title: Serial acquisition spending may be missing from sustainable owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.593 billion FY2025 acquisition payments, equal to 54.3% of the $2.9325 billion OE anchor and 39.6% of FY2025 OE; maintenance-like portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If acquisitions replace technology or supply growth embedded in the forecast, excluding their cash cost while adding back acquired-intangible amortization inflates sustainable OE and growth economics.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, cash provided by (used for) investing activities included net cash payments of $1.593 billion for acquisitions of multiple businesses, primarily related to Bolt Medical, SoniVie Ltd., Cortex, Inc., Intera, and Anrei Medical (HZ) Co., Ltd., and purchases of property, plant and equipment and internal use software of $876 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is an unresolved economic-classification issue rather than a demonstrated error because the record does not establish what portion of acquisitions is maintenance-like. Its filed scale is nevertheless large enough to change the valuation conclusion if a meaningful recurring portion is required, so it remains materially open.
audit_findings.action: Classify acquisition spending over a representative cycle into maintenance, growth and nonrecurring components; reconcile each component with acquired-intangible amortization and forecast growth, then rerun OE after deducting a normalized maintenance amount or retaining the corresponding amortization expense.

audit_findings.title: Uncapped contingent consideration is an additional claim on future cash flows
audit_findings.magnitude: $58 million filed fair value for uncapped consideration and $257 million total contingent-consideration liability at June 30, 2026; uncapped maximum unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Sales-based payments reduce cash available to common equity but may be absent from OE when settlements are classified as financing cash flows and absent from the stated bridge when the liability is not deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: The maximum amount for certain contingent consideration is not determinable as it is uncapped and based on a percent of certain sales.
audit_findings.explanation: The additional claim is demonstrated, and the filed $58 million estimate is only 0.13% of base equity value, while the entire $257 million liability is 0.58%. Those expected amounts alone are not material, but the uncapped sales-based obligation has no determinable maximum and its normalized cash burden is not supplied, so the record cannot establish that the exposure is immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Identify each uncapped agreement, applicable sales base, rate, duration and cash classification; project the normalized payments and either deduct their present liability in the bridge or deduct their cash cost from OE exactly once, then rerun if the resulting adjustment is material.

audit_findings.title: The share ceiling may omit maximum performance-award dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: Conservative maximum incremental dilution of 7.232 million shares if every included award unit doubled, equal to 0.49% of the 1,476.723 million-share denominator; approximately $0.15 per base-value share and $0.17 per bull-value share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any performance units above target increase the diluted share denominator and reduce value per share without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of RSUs ultimately granted under this program range from 0 percent to 200 percent of the target number of performance-based RSUs awarded to the participant as determined by achievement of the performance criteria of the program.
audit_findings.explanation: The denominator reconciliation is unresolved, but the filed 7.232 million total award units provides a conservative ceiling: even assuming every unit receives the additional 100% maximum payout, dilution is under 0.5%. That would reduce the reported scenario values by only about $0.12 to $0.17 per share and cannot bridge the $12.98 gap between market price and bull value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain target units outstanding separately for TSR and organic-growth awards, apply the applicable maximum or expected payout, and reconcile them to the 7.232 million units already included before updating the denominator.
